title: Search and Rescue
description:
Service members from the 81st ERQS, Expeditionary Rescue Squadron at Camp 
Lemonnier in Djibouti show and discuss the importance of the aircraft maintenance side of things, as they contribute to the overall mission of search and rescue.
keywords: Camp Lemonnier, Ramiro Gonzalez, Tavaris Scott, search and rescue, maintenance, CJTF-HOA, C-130
unit_name: Combined Joint Task Force - Horn of Africa

transcript.text: - We're the 81st ERQS, Experienced Rescue Squadron.
Our mission is personnel recovery and search and rescue.
Day in, day out, we come in and work.
For me, I get instructions from my pro-super, what we need
to do for the day, and I come out, get all my
maintainers out and about, and execute
what he needs done for the day, in a timely,
efficient way so we can keep the airplanes
safe and reliable throughout the day.
The importance of the maintenance mission is to
for us to keep the aircraft reliable and safe,
and at 100% at all times so we can go out
and do our mission of search and rescue
at any time and at short notice when we're called upon.
So, if we don't have that happening, planes are down,
and we can't do our mission and that potentially won't
save a life or whatever we have to do down the way.
- It's pretty much like working with a family.
Even though, we're working together, we have our days
when we're down but we still pick each other up and
say, "Hey man, we got a mission, we got to do it.
Let's get it together and let's get it done."
It's just something about, knowing that you
put your hard work, your sweat, blood, tears
into it and seeing that plane take off,
and you know that somebody is going to be rescued
safe and brought back home to see their families
and friends once again.
The most gratifying thing would probably be
seeing a plane take off.
I just love what I do and I'm glad that I'm allowed
to do it.
(airplane taking off)
